subject: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart & next steps

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart & next steps

Thanks again for the time today, Sarah — really enjoyed the conversation and demo. I wanted to send a quick recap with next steps and a couple of concrete items so your team can get started with the Hosted API evaluation this week.

Recap / recommended path:
- Hosted API is the fastest path for your POC: no infra to manage, quick SDKs, and easy token/key issuance.
- Typical quick evaluation covers authentication, basic endpoints (chat/generate + embeddings), and a short load test to validate latency at expected concurrency.

Questions we had on the call (please confirm):
- Expected sustained traffic for the POC: you mentioned ~5-10 req/s, with bursts up to ~50 concurrent users — is that still correct?
- Latency SLO target: you said ~200ms p95 for inference — confirm if p95 or p99.
- Data residency: you noted US-only, correct?

Quickstart & endpoints:
- Quickstart guide (attached): redwood-quickstart.pdf — contains SDK snippets and a one-line curl example.
- Hosted endpoints: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (chat/generate), https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
- Auth: API key in Authorization: Bearer <KEY> header.

Rate limits & bursting:
- Default hosted limits are 60 requests/second per API key and token-rate limits that depend on model and sequence length. For your demo we can provision a temporary burst to ~200 rps for a short window — will need to coordinate scheduling.

When to consider Dedicated / Private:
- Dedicated capacity is recommended for sustained throughput > 500 rps, long-running high-concurrency production, or when you want reserved GPU pools and an SLA-backed commitment.
- Private (VPC / on-prem) is for regulated data/privacy constraints or when you require customer-managed networking and full control over the control plane.

Next steps / asks:
1) Please confirm the POC targets above (sustained & burst traffic, latency SLO, data residency).
2) If you want a demo burst window, suggest 1-2 candidate dates/times and we'll reserve it.
3) Want a quick call with Dev to walk the team through the quickstart and set up keys? I can loop in Dev (cc'd) and Rishi from Solutions for any performance tuning.

I've attached the quickstart PDF and a small sample config for the demo burst. I'll follow up with a short checklist once you confirm.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Thanks for the quick answers, Sarah — that all helps. Quick clarifications and answers to your questions:

Rate limits:
- Default hosted limits are 60 requests/second per API key (burst smoothing applies). Token throughput limits vary by model; for typical chat models we recommend planning for ~1000 tokens/sec for medium requests.
- We can provision a demo burst: we've historically opened ~200 rps for a 2-4 hour demo window. If you confirm the webinar date/time we'll lock that in and notify infra.

Logs & retention:
- Request traces / logs are available in the Redwood Console (per-request latency, token counts, and input hashes). Default retention for request logs is 30 days for hosted plans; we can extend retention or provide a log export for audits.

Cost estimate:
- I attached a short hosted-estimate link above; I'll also drop a one-page estimate to your drive after this thread. For the POC your expected run-rate at 5-10 req/s with light context is roughly $X–$Y/month (I'll send a tailored sheet once you confirm expected average tokens per request).

Next steps I propose:
- Friday quickstart session (30-45m) with Dev and Rishi: I'm available 12:30pm ET or 3:00pm ET — which works for your team?
- Confirm webinar demo window (date/time) for us to provision the burst.
- If you want to test sustained higher throughput or run an engineering load test, we can discuss a short Dedicated evaluation (temporary reserved pool) but based on your targets Hosted should be fine.

I've attached a small config that Dev can drop into their test harness (acme-demo-burst-request.yaml). Dev / Rishi, can you confirm availability for the Friday slot and coordinate the burst provisioning if Sarah confirms the webinar time?

Best,
Marissa
